stem.en: Two organisms both have a true nucleus but are placed in different kingdoms. R is one cell that moves with flagella and makes food in light. Q has many cells in threads, a cell wall and no chlorophyll, and grows on dead matter. What separates them?

text.en: R lives in water and Q in soil, and habitat decides the kingdom.

feedback.en: Habitat is not one of the criteria for a kingdom.

text.en: R is unicellular and makes food; Q is multicellular and cannot.

feedback.en: Right. Number of cells and mode of nutrition place R in Protista and Q in Fungi.

text.en: R has a nucleus and Q has none, so only R is a eukaryote.

feedback.en: The question says that both have a true nucleus, so both are eukaryotes.

text.en: R has genetic material and Q has none, so only R is a true cell.

feedback.en: Every living cell has genetic material, in both R and Q.

explanation.en: Both are eukaryotes, so the next tests decide: R is unicellular and can make its own food, so it goes in Protista. Q is multicellular, with a wall and no chlorophyll, so it goes in Fungi.

hints.en: Both pass the nucleus test. Which other tests in the five kingdom system separate them?
